newsitem.title: UK: NatWest shares rise after BZW upgrade.
newsitem.headline: NatWest shares rise after BZW upgrade.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc firmed six pence to 716-1/2 by 1140 GMT after BZW moved its recommendation on the stock to "buy" from "hold", dealers said.
BZW banking analyst Hugh Pye confirmed the move but declined further comment.

NatWest shares have benefited from a series of positive recommendations in recent days. Panmure Gordon repeated a "buy" rating on NatWest on Monday while a repeated Credit Lyonnais Laing "buy" recommendation boosted the stock on Friday.
NatWest shares lagged the rest of the UK banking sector last year, with analysts blaming concerns about its strategy of expanding in investment banking and fund management through major acquisitions.
Other banking stocks were also mostly higher on Wednesday, helped by comment in the sector in the Financial Times Lex column which was modestly upbeat on its short-term prospects.
Despite looming risks from increasing competition, the FT said UK banks "continue to spew out cash... fuelling dividend growth around twice the market average."
Barclays Plc was up 9-1/2p at 10.25 stg, Lloyds TSB Group Plc was up 4p at 438 and Abbey National Plc was up 4p at 757.
HSBC Holdings Plc was up 7-1/2p at 13.23-1/2 stg, additionally benefitting from inclusion in Lehman Brothers' list of 19 continental European stocks the brokerage expects to outperform through 1997.
